newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan sees Q2 slowdown in US data - BusinessWeek.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan sees Q2 slowdown in US data - BusinessWeek.

text.p: Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan has said he expects a second-quarter economic slowdown, and U.S. markets appear to anticipate less credit tightening than they had in late March, an article in BusinessWeek said.
Greenspan told associates the Fed's 25-basis-point rate hike on March 25 may eventually seem unnecessary, the article in the May 12 edition of the magazine said.
The Fed chief saw recent economic data as supportive of his forecast for slower growth this quarter, even though Gross Domestic Product grew swiftly last quarter, it said.
Inventories growth provided much of the first-quarter surge in GDP, while orders for durable goods have declined. That combination may suggest economic softness in the months ahead, the article said.
The strong dollar and higher interest rates should also contribute to a slowdown, it said.
Impressive gains in stocks and bonds imply Wall Street expects the Fed will not have to tighten much more, if at all, BusinessWeek said.
But Fed Governor Laurence Meyer said the central bank will hike rates again "as long as growth is above-trend and (factory) utilization rates are rising," it said.
